Recommend and run a causal-discovery method for a data set

Source: R/auto.R
cd_auto.Rd

Inspects a data set with cd_diagnose()'s transparent characteristics, routes it to a discovery method suited to that regime, runs the best installed method on the route, and returns the recovered graph together with the routing rationale and a confidence label. Because causal discovery has no run-time ground truth, this is a recommender, not a selector: it reports why it chose and how sure it is, and – in "consensus" mode – returns a stability-weighted union of several methods with per-edge agreement.

Usage

cd_auto(
  data,
  mode = c("route", "consensus"),
  report = TRUE,
  top_k = 3L,
  threshold = 0.05,
  density_components = 4L
)

Arguments

data

A numeric matrix or data frame of observations by variables, an evaluable-density object (a proxymix gmm / gmm_fit / gmm_target), or a sufficient statistic (cd_suffstat()).

mode

"route" (run the single recommended method) or "consensus" (run the top top_k installed methods on the route and return their stability-weighted union).

report

A single logical. When TRUE (the default) the recommended method is run and its graph returned; when FALSE only the recommendation is returned, with an empty graph and the status "recommendation only (report = FALSE)".

top_k

The number of methods to combine in "consensus" mode.

threshold

The partial-correlation edge threshold for the density route.

density_components

The number of mixture components to fit when routing an evaluable target density.

Value

A cd_result whose rationale, confidence, and alternatives (always a list of method labels, in the route's preference order) record the recommendation. In "consensus" mode the per-edge agreement and the individual member results are stored in the result's provenance (as agreement and runs).

Details

The route is decided by four data-characteristic thresholds, checked in this order and reported in the result's provenance$thresholds: a curvature heuristic above 0.05 routes to a kernel conditional-independence test; a non-Gaussian margin fraction of 0.5 or more routes to the LiNGAM family; a correlation condition number above 1000 (a latent-structure hint) routes to a confounder-robust method; and a residual-variance ratio below 2 routes to the equal-variance continuous-optimisation methods. Failing all four, the benchmark's strongest overall method is used.

When data is an evaluable density rather than a sample – a proxymix gmm, gmm_fit, or gmm_target (requires the suggested proxymix package) – the conditional-independence (Markov) structure is read off the mixture in closed form, the route for the case where a density can be evaluated but not sampled.

When data is a sufficient statistic (cd_suffstat(), a correlation matrix and its sample size), the recommender routes among the sufficient-statistic methods. A correlation matrix carries only the latent-structure hint, so the rationale states plainly that the non-Gaussianity, nonlinearity, and equal-variance tests could not be run.

See also

cd_diagnose(), cd_discover(), list_methods()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pcalg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sim <- cd_scenario("linear_laplace", seed = 1)
  rec <- cd_auto(sim$data, report = FALSE)
  rec@rationale
}
#> [1] "100% of variables depart from normality (mean |excess kurtosis| 1.41); the LiNGAM family exploits non-Gaussianity for orientation and is fast"
